bugs: Validation runs before Gate::authorize in update, so a non-author sending invalid data gets 422, not 403 (PostController.php:36-38).
antipatterns: app/Models/Post.php:45-54: scopes take nullable arguments and do the when() internally, so withStatus(null) silently does nothing. That is a surprising scope contract; the conditional belongs at the call site.

app/Http/Requests/SavePostRequest.php:16: switching rules on isMethod('POST') is a terse but implicit way to share one request between store and update.
tests/Feature/Api/PostTest.php:106: substring message assertions such as '255' and 'array' are loose.

v.rationale: All three tests suites pass (impl-2: 20, impl-3: 24, impl-1: 26). They share the same core design: enum cast, #[Fillable]/#[ObservedBy]/#[Scope] attributes, an observer for the unique slug and published_at, a policy using user()->is(), and apiResource without show. My probes found the same behaviour in all three: blank tags return 422, title:null returns 422, an all-symbol title gets slug 'post' then 'post-2', client-supplied published_at/user_id are ignored, and an array passed to the filters returns 422. All three also validate before authorizing, so a non-author sending invalid data gets 422 instead of 403. Unauthenticated non-JSON requests return 500 (no login route) in all three; that comes from the base app. What separates them: impl-2 puts the 'web' middleware group on API routes, which brings in CSRF (PreventRequestForgery). The tests hide this because CSRF is skipped under unit tests, but real token-less JSON clients would get 419. impl-2 also has an awkward UpdatePostRequest that extends the store request and plucks parent::rules()['status'], and its trimming repeats TrimStrings, so it ranks last. impl-3 has the strongest tests and a very thin controller. Against that, its scopes take nullable arguments and no-op on null, syncTagNames mixes a side effect with a returned eager-load, and duplicate tags are silently dropped. impl-1 is the cleanest idiomatically: $request->enum(), ??= in the observer, slug route binding, 'sometimes','required' plus 'distinct' for explicit 422s, and a policy whose delete delegates to update. Its only real flaws are minor ceremony (a postAttributes() helper copied into both requests, Http::preventStrayRequests, a trivial cast test), so it ranks first, narrowly ahead of impl-3.
